## What's new in 0.1.0-preview.1
This first preview makes the console easier to read and safe for logs, makes the GUI show what it is doing while it starts, and fixes problems with searches, email notifications, settings files and data folders. Your settings, search files, campground list and `Camp.History` keep working as they are; "Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta.10" below lists the few cases where something now behaves differently.

### Correct results when several searches run together
- Each search now gets exactly the results it would get if it ran on its own. Before, when several searches ran at the same time and at least one of them used `consecutiveDays`, a search could show two-night openings that don't exist, leave out valid results, show campsites of another campground, or keep email mode from sending a notification. This was a known limitation of 0.1.0-beta.10.
- A search that ran correctly on its own finds the same results as before; nothing that matches your search is left out.

### Dates that don't depend on your regional settings
- The dates Campertron works out itself (for `DaysOut`, `MonthsOut` and `Until` searches, and the months it asks recreation.gov for) no longer depend on your computer's regional settings. Before, with settings that write the day first, such as UK or German settings, a search could stop with an error like "… was not recognized as a valid DateTime", and with settings that use another calendar, such as Persian, Campertron could ask for the wrong month.
- Dates you write yourself in `searchValueDates` are still read with your regional settings. Write them as `yyyy-MM-dd`, for example `2026-11-20`; the examples page in the repository explains why.

### Email mode keeps searching the right dates
- When email mode runs for days, `DaysOut`, `MonthsOut` and `Until` searches now move forward with the calendar, so every check searches from that day on. Before, the dates were worked out once at the start: a `DaysOut 30` search covered one day less each day and nothing at all after 30 days, without any warning.
- Dates you write yourself keep their meaning, and the search files are still read once, when Campertron starts.

### Email notifications only for emails that were sent
- Email mode now records a campsite and date in `Camp.History` only after the email that shows it has been sent successfully. Before, a check recorded everything it found before sending, so if the email failed (for example because `Email.yaml` was still empty, the server refused the connection or the password was wrong), those openings were never emailed.
- If one email of a check fails, the emails sent before it keep their record, and the openings of the failed email and of the emails after it are reported again when Campertron is started again. Campertron stops after a failed email with a message and exit code 1.
- `Camp.History` now appears only when the first campsite and date is recorded. Console and HtmlFile searches, and email checks with nothing new, no longer create an empty `Camp.History` folder.
- The history's format is unchanged. A check whose emails all go out records exactly what it recorded before, and existing history is kept.

### Your search files stay as you wrote them
- Campertron creates the example search `ZionConfig.yaml` only when the settings folder has no search file at all. Before, if none of your search files had `autoRun: true`, Campertron wrote the example over a `ZionConfig.yaml` of your own, losing its values and comments, and then ran the example.
- If you have search files but none of them has `autoRun: true`, Campertron leaves them exactly as they are, shows "No search file has autoRun: true, so no search runs." and searches nothing. In email mode it keeps running and reports "0 searches" at every check; set `autoRun: true` in a search file and restart Campertron to search again.
- An empty `General.yaml` or search file, or one that contains only comments, now gets a clear error that names the file and says what to do, and Campertron exits with code 1. Before, it stopped with an "Object reference not set to an instance of an object" error. The file is left as it is, and an empty search file is never replaced by the example. An empty `Email.yaml` is still accepted when you don't use email mode.
- A `StartEndDate` search whose start and end date are the same is now reported like any other unusable search file: one error that names the file, exit code 1, and no waiting for a key press. Before, Campertron waited for a key and then exited with code 0, or crashed when it had no keyboard input. Equal dates are still not a valid search.

### Safer data folders
- On Linux, if `~/.local/share` (or the folder set in `XDG_DATA_HOME`) doesn't exist yet, Campertron now creates it and keeps its data there. Before, it put `CampertronConfig` and `CampertronCache`, including the campground list of about 226 MB, into whichever folder it was started from. Existing folders, Windows, macOS and the Docker image's `/config` and `/cache` are not affected.
- Refreshing the campground list now unpacks the download into a folder of Campertron's own, `CampertronExtract`, next to `CampertronConfig` and `CampertronCache`, and removes only that folder afterwards. Before, it used a folder simply called `Extract` in the same place and deleted it, which could have removed another program's folder of that name.

### A clearer console
- **Results are easier to read.** Single nights are grouped by date, and consecutive nights by campsite with their dates in order. Check-in and check-out times and equipment are shown once when they are the same for every site, and a summary line ends the run, for example "Done: 2 searches, 10 openings at 4 sites." The calendar marks open days with `*` as well as with color.
- **You see what is searched.** Before searching, the console lists your searches with their campground, dates, weekdays and number of people, and warns about any search that can't find anything as written, for example one without a `campgroundID` or with an ID that isn't in the campground list. During a search from the menu, each search reports when it is done with one "Checked …" line.
- **Messages you can act on.** Warnings and errors go to the error output and start with "Warning:" or "Error:". When Campertron can't continue, it says what went wrong and exits with code 1 instead of crashing: for a settings file it names the file and what to do, with the line and column when the file can't be read, and an email error never shows your password. Started without an interactive terminal, the menu says so and exits with code 1 instead of crashing.
- **Safe for logs.** Color is used only in a terminal, and the `NO_COLOR` environment variable turns it off. Redirected output and container logs contain plain text without control sequences. The screen is cleared without erasing your scrollback, and never while a message you haven't seen yet is on it.
- **Email mode writes a readable log.** It starts with one line naming the version, the .NET version and the folders, lists your searches once, then writes one timestamped line per check and per email, and no longer clears the screen.
- **Failed requests are reported.** A failed, busy or blocked request to recreation.gov is reported together with what happens next; Campertron retries as before.
- **View Config** is now a screen of its own. It also shows the Campertron version, where results go and the number of search files, and it says in plain words how long ago the campground list was refreshed.

### A GUI that shows what it is doing
- The window opens right away and shows "Preparing campground data" while Campertron sets up the campground list, for example on the first start. Before, no window appeared until that work was done.
- If that fails, for example because `General.yaml` can't be read, the window stays open and shows the problem (with the line and column for a settings error), the settings folder, what to do and a **Try again** button. Before, the GUI crashed without showing a window.
- If you close the window while the campground list is still being prepared, Campertron finishes that work before it exits.
- The campground details scroll from anywhere in the tab, also in very wide windows, where the mouse wheel used to do nothing beside them. Focus outlines no longer touch the text, the lists show "Select or type …" because you can type the first letters of a name to jump to it, and the GUI calls itself "Campertron" instead of "Avalonia Application".

### Checks before publishing
The release workflow must pass all of the following before it can publish this release; if any of them fails, nothing is published:
- all automated tests, and a scan that finds no known vulnerable packages;
- every download contains .NET 11, and all 16 downloads were compiled by the same .NET 11 compiler;
- on Linux x64, Windows x64, Windows on ARM, macOS on Intel and macOS on Apple silicon, the console and GUI downloads are started: the console's version check and a first start that sets up the campground list, and the GUI's built-in smoke test (window, campground data, clean close). Earlier releases started only the Linux x64 programs;
- the amd64 Docker image starts;
- the checksums of all 16 downloads are generated and verified.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta.10
- **Desktop:** extract the new archive and use it instead of your old Campertron folder. Your settings, searches, campground list and `Camp.History` (in the `CampertronConfig` data folder) are kept and need no changes.
- **Docker:** change the image tag to `0.1.0-preview.1` and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts. There is no `latest` tag for pre-release versions, so the tag has to be changed by hand.
- **Exit codes:** after "Blocked by API for exceeding request limit", Campertron still waits 5 minutes, but it now exits with code 1 instead of 0, so a service or container that restarts only on failure (for example systemd's `Restart=on-failure` or Docker's `--restart on-failure`) starts it again. A `StartEndDate` search with equal dates and the other failures described above also exit with code 1. Scripts that check Campertron's exit code now see these as failures.
- **If your data was in the folder you started Campertron from (Linux):** earlier versions did that when `~/.local/share` didn't exist. This version uses `~/.local/share` (or `XDG_DATA_HOME`) instead and doesn't move anything. Move your `CampertronConfig` folder there before you start this version; otherwise Campertron starts with new settings and, in email mode, an empty `Camp.History`. You can delete the old `CampertronCache` folder; Campertron builds a new one.
- **If you use email mode:** earlier versions recorded what a check found even when its email then failed, so those campsites and dates count as reported and won't be emailed. To be emailed about everything that is open again, delete the `Camp.History` folder in your settings folder while Campertron is not running.
- **If none of your search files has `autoRun: true`:** Campertron no longer replaces `ZionConfig.yaml` with the example and runs it; set `autoRun: true` in the searches you want to run.
- To check your download, use the checksums and build attestations described under "Verify your download" below.

## Known limitations
- **Console on Windows and macOS.** The new console layout, colors and menu were checked in Linux terminals. On Windows they had a manual visual check, not a complete test, and on macOS they haven't been tried yet. The checks before publishing start the console on those systems only for its version check and a first start that prints nothing.
- **Email settings are checked only when an email is sent.** Email mode doesn't check `Email.yaml` before it starts searching. With the empty `Email.yaml` that Campertron creates, the first check that finds something stops with an error when it tries to send; what it found is emailed once `Email.yaml` is filled in, if it is still open. Fill in `Email.yaml` before you switch to `outputTo: Email`.
- **Email clients not yet checked.** The results page was checked in Chrome and Firefox on Linux, but no test email was sent, so its appearance in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail is unverified. Some email programs, such as desktop Outlook, ignore much of the page's styling; the page is designed to stay readable without it. Each email contains the page twice (as the body and as the attachment), so a search with thousands of results can make a large email that some providers may reject.
- **Duplicate campground names:** a small number of campground names are not unique. In those cases, the GUI may show the ID of a different campground with the same name.
- Avalonia, the GUI's UI framework, lists 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) as a commercially supported platform only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`). Campertron still builds and publishes both GUI downloads, but neither is tested on a real device.
